context_notes:
Phase 38 is planned, heavily remediated, and committed, but ZERO plans have executed and NO GitHub state has been mutated by this phase: no alert dismissed, no branch deleted, no protection changed, no workflow removed. The repo is exactly where it was at the start of the session apart from planning documents.

This session was two full execution-gate runs and five remediation passes, and the gate earned its keep twice. Run 1 refuted the claim that 26 dismissals were per-alert justified: one reason string was pasted over 19 alerts and was factually false for at least 16, verified against four real test files. Run 2 refuted the origin/dev delete twice over: first the safety proof failed open when an empty shell variable made 'git rev-list --count origin/master..$DEVSHA' silently degrade to origin/master..HEAD and exit 0, then the PowerShell translation of the guard turned out to be strictly weaker than its POSIX source because a bare throw does not terminate across a submission boundary. That second one was reproduced with a control experiment: wrapper on, delete unreachable across 27 failure runs; wrapper stripped, same inputs, four guards fire and the delete runs anyway.

The two highest-stakes claims survived every attack at high confidence. There is no real credential leak hiding in the dismissal set: SARIF codeFlows root every clear-text finding at core/credentials.py:47, which is 20 credential key NAMES, and none root at an env read, a config field, or store.get(). And there is no merge lockout: the required CodeQL context is produced by default setup (app_id 57789, workflow 325304050), not by the codeql-analysis.yml file 38-03 deletes, which is already disabled_manually with zero runs.

The pattern worth carrying: every defect this session was found by measuring rather than reading. The false dismissal reason was caught by opening the four test files. The failed guard was caught by feeding the block to a real parser line by line. The stale cross-reference was caught by diffing two documents that were edited in parallel. Phase 38's remaining work is where that matters most, because a dismissal is indistinguishable from a fix in the alert count and the record cannot be edited afterward.
